posts.title: A backup you have never restored is a guess
posts.excerpt: Why we restore one folder for every client each month, and what we found this year.
posts.content:
Every month our engineers pick one folder from each client backup and restore it to a test machine. It takes twenty minutes and it is the only way to know a backup works.

This year the test caught three backups that had silently stopped after a password change. All three were fixed the same day, before anyone needed them.

posts.title: Moving a 34-person office over one weekend
posts.excerpt: Network, phones and every desk ready by Monday 8:00.
posts.content:
An accounting firm moved two floors across town on a Friday evening. We labelled every cable, moved the server at 19:00 and tested each desk on Sunday afternoon.

On Monday morning thirty-four people signed in at their new desks; the only call to the help desk was about a chair.

posts.title: Multi-factor sign-in, now on for every user
posts.excerpt: All 4,200 people we support now sign in with a second step.
posts.content:
Since September every account we look after asks for a second step at sign-in: an app prompt, or a key for staff who share a computer.

Stolen passwords remain the most common way into a small office. A second step stops almost all of those attempts.
